claims.text: The Pulumi `protect` resource option is a Pulumi-engine construct enforced entirely within Pulumi and never sent to the cloud provider.
Many cloud resources carry their own separate deletion-protection attributes, such as `deletionProtection` on a GCP Cloud SQL instance or an AWS RDS instance.
Cloud provider deletion-protection attributes (e.g. `deletionProtection` on GCP Cloud SQL or AWS RDS instances) are enforced by the cloud provider independently of Pulumi's `protect` option.
A resource can be unprotected in Pulumi and still refuse to delete due to provider deletion protection, or be protected in Pulumi while the provider's deletion protection is off.

The Pulumi docs page at /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/destroy-failures/ has a section 'Deletion protection on the resource itself' explaining how to tell Pulumi protect and provider deletion protection apart and resolve each.
Many cloud resources carry their own deletion-protection attributes, separate from Pulumi's `protect` resource option, which the provider or the cloud API enforces independently.
`deletionProtection` is a deletion-protection attribute on a GCP Cloud SQL instance (Pulumi gcp.sql.DatabaseInstance).
`deletionProtection` is a deletion-protection attribute on an AWS RDS instance (Pulumi aws.rds.Instance).
Pulumi's `protect` resource option and a resource's own provider-level deletion protection are complementary rather than substitutes for one another.

The Pulumi docs page destroy-failures has a section 'Deletion protection on the resource itself' explaining how to tell `protect` and resource-level deletion protection apart and resolve a destroy failure caused by either.
Pulumi's `protect` resource option is an engine-level guard that never reaches the cloud provider.
The Pulumi docs page /docs/iac/concepts/resources/options/protect/ exists and explains how to remove the `protect` option.

Some Pulumi providers refuse to issue the delete call when a resource carries a deletion-protection attribute, e.g. `deletionProtection` on `gcp.sql.DatabaseInstance` and `gcp.container.Cluster`; the failure surfaces from the provider before any request reaches the cloud API.
AWS RDS `deletionProtection`, EC2 `disableApiTermination`, and Azure Resource Manager management locks are cloud-API-enforced protections that reject the delete call independent of Pulumi.
Azure management lock errors often come back from the API with an error code such as `ScopeLocked`.
`pulumi destroy` deletes what is recorded in the stack's state, not what the program currently says, so setting the attribute to false in the program alone is not enough.
Remediation: set the deletion-protection attribute to false in the program, run `pulumi up` so the change reaches the live resource and state, then run `pulumi destroy`.
If protection was already disabled outside Pulumi, `pulumi refresh` synchronizes state with reality and `pulumi destroy` then succeeds without an intervening `pulumi up`.
`gcp.sql.DatabaseInstance` has a provider-enforced `deletionProtection` attribute, and a nested `settings.deletionProtectionEnabled` also guards the instance at the GCP API level.
`gcp.container.Cluster` has a provider-enforced `deletionProtection` attribute.
`gcp.bigquery.Table` has a provider-enforced `deletionProtection` attribute.
`gcp.bigquery.Dataset` has a `deleteContentsOnDestroy` attribute; destroying a dataset that still contains tables fails unless it is true.
`aws.rds.Instance` and `aws.rds.Cluster` have a `deletionProtection` attribute enforced by the AWS API that defaults to false.
`aws.s3.BucketV2` has a `forceDestroy` attribute that defaults to false; a non-empty bucket otherwise fails to delete.
`aws.ec2.Instance` has a `disableApiTermination` attribute enforced by the AWS API (EC2 termination protection).
`aws.dynamodb.Table` has a `deletionProtectionEnabled` attribute enforced by the AWS API that defaults to false.

In azure-native, `azure-native.authorization.ManagementLockByScope` and scope-specific variants such as `ManagementLockAtResourceLevel` exist; Azure Resource Manager enforces a `CanNotDelete` lock, which must be removed before the resource can be deleted, independent of the Pulumi program.

Destroying an `azure-native.keyvault.Vault` only soft-deletes it; recreating a vault with the same name fails with `VaultAlreadyExists` until the soft-deleted vault is purged or recovered, and purge protection prevents purging until its retention period elapses.
